mainTopic: Does רבי יוסי treat עבודה זרה differently from other prohibitions when a forbidden thing and a permitted thing together produce a result (זה וזה גורם)?
overview: The amud opens with the end of a source: growth from planting, sinking or grafting an ערלה tree is permitted, which shows that רבי יוסי allows a result caused by a forbidden and a permitted thing together (זה וזה גורם). The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי might be stricter with עבודה זרה. It challenges this with two ברייתות that disagree about a field fertilized with עבודה זרה dung and a cow fattened on עבודה זרה vetches. To save the suggestion, the גמרא tries to give the ברייתות to רבי אליעזר and the רבנן instead. First it points to their dispute about leaven of תרומה, but that fails because רבי אליעזר may simply follow the last leaven. Then it points to their dispute about bread baked with אשרה wood, but no group of רבנן can be the lenient side. So the גמרא concludes that the lenient ברייתא is רבי יוסי after all. It explains that his strict-sounding ruling in the משנה was said only according to the רבנן's view, and shows how the רבנן answer him using רב מרי's rule. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and רב יוסף applies this to a real garden fertilized with עבודה זרה dung.

steps.title: Planting, sinking or grafting gives permitted growth
steps.stepSummary: The end of a cited source: if someone planted, sank or grafted from an ערלה tree, what grows is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that if one planted, sank a shoot into the ground, or grafted, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a source. It says that new growth coming from a forbidden ערלה source planted in permitted ground is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new growth has two causes, the forbidden ערלה material and the permitted ground, and the result is still permitted. This is the idea of זה וזה גורם, which the next steps tie to רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: planted
sank a branch into the ground so it roots (layering)
grafted
permitted
fruit of a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit

phrases.english: that if one planted, or sank a shoot, or grafted, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a quote that started before this line. The planted things come from an ערלה tree, and the new growth is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a source quoted just before this section begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Growth that comes from a forbidden ערלה source together with permitted ground is permitted.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי is stricter with עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way out: perhaps רבי יוסי treats עבודה זרה differently from other prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that רבי יוסי distinguishes between other prohibitions and עבודה זרה…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible defense: רבי יוסי's leniency might apply only to ordinary prohibitions, not to עבודה זרה. It is setting this idea up so it can test it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי's rule of זה וזה גורם applies only to things like ערלה, then a strict ruling about עבודה זרה would not contradict him. The 'וכי תימא' wording shows this is a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
it is different for him; he makes a distinction
other prohibitions

phrases.english: And if you would say,
Rabbi Yosei makes a distinction
between other prohibitions and idol worship,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a limit on how far רבי יוסי's leniency reaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seemed to contradict himself: he is lenient with זה וזה גורם (as in the ערלה case of step 1), yet strict about planting under an אשרה in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: רבי יוסי is lenient only with other prohibitions, not with עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Two ברייתות about dung and vetches of idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggested distinction by quoting two ברייתות that disagree about a field and a cow that benefited from עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really distinguish? But it was taught: a field fertilized with dung of עבודה זרה, and likewise a cow fattened on vetches of עבודה זרה. One ברייתא says the field may be sown and the cow slaughtered. Another says the field must lie fallow and the cow must be made lean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks, 'Does he really make that distinction?' and brings two ברייתות that rule opposite ways on the same עבודה זרה cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases a permitted thing (the field, the cow) and a forbidden thing (the dung, the vetches) together produce the result. That is exactly a זה וזה גורם case, but here it involves עבודה זרה. The lenient ברייתא lets the produce and the meat be used. The strict one waits until the forbidden effect is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: but does he really distinguish? (opens a challenge)
was fertilized with dung
vetches, a kind of animal feed
should be left fallow, unplanted
should be made lean

phrases.english: But does he really distinguish?
But isn't it taught:
a field that was fertilized with dung of idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן פָּרָה שֶׁנִּתְפַּטְּמָה בְּכַרְשִׁינֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: and likewise a cow that was fattened with vetches of idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: שָׂדֶה תִּזָּרַע, פָּרָה תִּשָּׁחֵט,
phrases.english: one baraita teaches: the field may be sown, the cow may be slaughtered,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: שָׂדֶה תָּבוֹר, וּפָרָה תִּרְזֶה.
phrases.english: and another teaches: the field should lie fallow, and the cow should be made lean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction suggested in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יוסי treats עבודה זרה more strictly than other prohibitions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a known dispute about זה וזה גורם that involves עבודה זרה itself. If the lenient side of it is רבי יוסי, he is lenient even with עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The lenient ברייתא must be רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the lenient ברייתא follows רבי יוסי and the strict one follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that this one is רבי יוסי and that one is the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge by matching the lenient ברייתא to רבי יוסי and the strict one to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this matching is right, רבי יוסי allows a זה וזה גורם result even in an עבודה זרה case. That would knock out the distinction from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not that…? (proposes a reading as a challenge)
the Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: What, is it not that this one is Rabbi Yosei,
and that one is the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge by naming who holds each ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יוסי is stricter with עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Matching the lenient ברייתא to רבי יוסי shows he is lenient in an עבודה זרה case too.

steps.title: No, the dispute is רבי אליעזר and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the matching: the two ברייתות follow רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, not רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. This one is רבי אליעזר, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge and gives the two ברייתות to different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the dispute is moved to רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, it no longer tells us anything about רבי יוסי. So the distinction from step 2 can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: no (rejects the proposed reading)

phrases.english: No, this one is Rabbi Eliezer,
and that one is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 3 and 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the lenient ברייתא is רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות can be explained as a different dispute, between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.title: Which dispute of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which known disagreement between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן explains the two ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which dispute of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the answer from step 5 to point to a specific dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן that fits these cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to name two disputing sides. The גמרא wants an actual known dispute whose reasoning matches the field and cow cases.

keyTerms.meaning: which?

phrases.english: Which dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details on the answer given in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which known dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן the two ברייתות reflect.

steps.title: First suggestion: the dispute about leaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes a first suggestion: the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about שאור (leaven).
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the dispute of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about leaven…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer, the dispute about שאור. The word 'אילימא' tells us it is about to show why this answer does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אילימא' brings in a suggestion only so it can be tested and usually turned down. Steps 8–9 quote the leaven משנה and אביי's reading of it, and step 10 shows why it does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (brings in a suggestion that will likely be rejected)
leaven, sourdough starter

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. 'אילימא' means the leaven dispute is being suggested and will be shown not to fit.

phrases.english: If we say it is the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis about leaven…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first, temporary answer to the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggestion, still to be tested: the dispute about leaven.

steps.title: The משנה about leaven of תרומה and חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in ערלה about two pieces of leaven, one of חולין and one of תרומה. Neither one alone could make the dough rise, but together they did. רבי אליעזר follows the last one that fell in. The חכמים say the dough is forbidden only if the תרומה leaven alone was strong enough to make it rise.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Leaven of חולין and leaven of תרומה fell into a dough. Neither one alone was enough to make it rise, but together they made it rise. רבי אליעזר says: I go after the last one. The חכמים say: whether the forbidden leaven fell in first or last, the dough is not forbidden unless the forbidden leaven alone was enough to make it rise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the source for its suggestion from step 7: the משנה where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about leaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case two causes, one permitted (חולין) and one forbidden (תרומה), work together to make the dough rise. The חכמים clearly allow the dough unless the תרומה alone could have done the job. רבי אליעזר's view, 'I follow the last one,' still needs explaining. אביי does that in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Sourdough leaven, used to make dough rise
Ordinary food that is not sacred and is permitted to everyone
The portion given to a כהן; forbidden to a non-כהן
To make the dough rise (become leavened)
They combined, joined together
I follow the last one (the last thing that fell in decides)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'forbidden' (אסור) means forbidden to a non-כהן because it is תרומה. It does not mean forbidden to everyone. The case is a model for any situation where a permitted thing and a forbidden thing together cause one result.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: שְׂאוֹר שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
phrases.english: As we learned: leaven of non-sacred produce and of תרומה
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in ערלה 2:11.

phrases.english: that fell into a dough,
and this one alone was not enough to make it rise,
and that one alone was not enough to make it rise,
but they combined and made it rise.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַר הָאַחֲרוֹן אֲנִי בָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: I go after the last one,
phrases.notes: He means whichever leaven fell in last decides the status of the dough.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בֵּין שֶׁנָּפַל אִיסּוּר לְכִתְחִלָּה
phrases.english: and the Sages say: whether the forbidden one fell in first
or whether the forbidden one fell in last,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ.
phrases.english: it is not forbidden unless it alone has enough to make it rise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה that step 7 pointed to as the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about a result caused by both a permitted and a forbidden thing, which would explain the two ברייתות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה ערלה 2:11: the leaven of חולין and תרומה that together made a dough rise.

steps.title: אביי explains רבי אליעזר: the forbidden leaven must be removed first
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי אליעזר permits the dough when the permitted leaven fell in last only if the forbidden leaven was taken out first. If it was not removed, the dough is forbidden. So רבי אליעזר seems to hold that when a permitted and a forbidden thing together cause a result, the result is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: They taught this only when he first removed the forbidden leaven. But if he did not first remove the forbidden leaven, the dough is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings אביי's explanation of רבי אליעזר. This completes the suggestion that רבי אליעזר forbids things caused by both permitted and forbidden causes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, when both leavens are still in the dough working together, רבי אליעזר forbids it. That is the rule of זה וזה גורם אסור. The חכמים permit it, so this would match the strict ברייתא to רבי אליעזר and the lenient one to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of...
He first removed (took out beforehand)
This and that cause it: a result caused by both a permitted and a forbidden thing

steps.whyThisMatters: With אביי's reading, the leaven dispute becomes a dispute about זה וזה גורם. That is exactly what is needed to explain the two ברייתות about the field and the cow.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: They taught this only
phrases.notes: He is explaining when רבי אליעזר allows the dough because the permitted leaven fell in last.

phrases.english: where he first removed the forbidden leaven,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא קָדַם וְסִילֵּק אֶת הָאִיסּוּר — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if he did not first remove the forbidden leaven, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁקָּדַם וְסִילֵּק אֶת הָאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds אביי's explanation of רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה, so that it shows his position on זה וזה גורם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the dough is permitted when the permitted leaven fell in last only if the forbidden leaven was removed first. Otherwise it is forbidden, which means זה וזה גורם אסור.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אליעזר simply follows the last leaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know רבי אליעזר's reason is the one אביי gives. Maybe his reason is just what he said, 'I follow the last one.' If the forbidden leaven finished the rising, the dough is forbidden. If the permitted leaven finished it, the dough is permitted, whether or not the forbidden leaven was removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But from where do we know that רבי אליעזר's reason is like אביי's? Maybe רבי אליעזר's reason is because he said 'I follow the last one.' If the rising was finished by the forbidden leaven, it is forbidden. If it was finished by the permitted leaven, it is permitted, whether or not he removed the forbidden one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the leaven dispute. רבי אליעזר's view might have nothing to do with זה וזה גורם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reading is not forced. רבי אליעזר may hold that only the last leaven counts, so removing the forbidden leaven makes no difference. In that case the leaven dispute does not show that he forbids זה וזה גורם, and it cannot explain the two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know? (questions an assumption)
Perhaps
Was completed, finished (the rising was finished by)
He removed it

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying אביי is wrong about the הלכה. It only says his reading is not the only possible way to understand רבי אליעזר, so it cannot prove anything here.

phrases.english: But from where do we know that Rabbi Eliezer's reason is like Abaye's?
Perhaps Rabbi Eliezer's reason
is because of 'I go after the last one,'
if the rising was finished by the forbidden leaven, it is forbidden,
and if it was finished by the permitted leaven, they are permitted,
whether he removed it or did not remove it!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the forbidden leaven. On this reading, taking it out makes no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the use of אביי's explanation, and with it the first suggestion from step 7 that the leaven dispute explains the two ברייתות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the first suggestion from step 7, that the leaven dispute is the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן behind the two ברייתות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's view can be read as simply 'the last leaven decides,' whether or not the forbidden leaven was removed. On that reading his view says nothing about זה וזה גורם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי אליעזר's reason in the leaven משנה follows אביי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another simple reading of רבי אליעזר's own words, 'I follow the last one,' that does not need אביי's condition.

steps.title: A new suggestion: the dispute about wood
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the שאור idea, the גמרא suggests that the two ברייתות follow the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about wood from an אשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the two ברייתות match the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first idea and offers a second one. It points to a different dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, about wood. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שאור case did not clearly show what רבי אליעזר holds, because his reason might simply be 'I follow the last one.' So the גמרא looks for another case where he and the רבנן argue, hoping this one shows his view about something caused by both a forbidden thing and a permitted thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier idea is dropped and a new one is coming.
Wood. Here it means wood taken from an אשרה, a tree that was worshipped.

phrases.english: Rather,
it is the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis about wood.
phrases.notes: This is the wood of an אשרה, a tree that was worshipped. The משנה quoted next explains it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected שאור suggestion (steps 7–10) with a new candidate dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about wood from an אשרה is the source for the two ברייתות.

steps.title: The משנה about wood from an אשרה: oven and bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: wood taken from an אשרה is forbidden for benefit. A new oven fired with it must be broken, and an old one must be allowed to cool. Bread baked with it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone took wood from an אשרה, it is forbidden for any benefit. If he heated an oven with it, a new oven must be smashed, and an old oven must be allowed to cool. If he baked bread with it, the bread is forbidden for any benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה it pointed to. This first part sets up the basic rules before the dispute comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new oven is strengthened by its first firing, so the forbidden wood gave it a lasting benefit, and it must be broken. An old oven gains only the heat, so waiting until it cools is enough. The bread is forbidden because it was baked with forbidden wood, even though the oven itself was permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden for any benefit, not only for eating.
He heated or fired, meaning he lit a fire in it.
It must be smashed or broken.
It must be allowed to cool down.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If he took wood from it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the אשרה, the worshipped tree.

phrases.english: it is forbidden for benefit.
If he heated the oven with it:
a new oven must be smashed,
an old oven must be cooled.
If he baked bread with it,
the bread is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that step 11 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that the wood dispute is the basis for the two ברייתות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עבודה זרה (49b) about wood from an אשרה.

steps.title: The dispute about bread that got mixed in
steps.stepSummary: If the forbidden bread got mixed with other bread, the רבנן forbid all of it. רבי אליעזר says to throw the value of the benefit into ים המלח. The רבנן answer that there is no redemption for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the bread got mixed with other loaves, all of them are forbidden for benefit. רבי אליעזר says: He should take the value of the benefit and throw it into the Dead Sea. They said to him: There is no redemption for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the dispute itself, the part the גמרא needs. רבי אליעזר offers a way out by destroying the value of the forbidden wood, and the רבנן reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר does not say the bread is simply permitted. He requires the value of the wood to be destroyed. That suggests he sees the bread as forbidden because of the wood, even though a permitted oven also helped bake it. This is why the גמרא thinks he matches the ברייתא that forbids something caused by a forbidden thing together with a permitted thing.

keyTerms.meaning: It got mixed in.
The Dead Sea, the place where something is thrown so it is destroyed for good.
Redemption, meaning freeing something by paying its value.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not being more lenient about whether the bread is affected by the forbidden wood. He agrees the wood's benefit must be removed. He only allows removing it by destroying its value instead of destroying all the bread.

phrases.english: If it got mixed with others,
phrases.notes: The forbidden loaf got mixed in with other, permitted loaves.

phrases.english: all of them are forbidden for benefit.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He should take the benefit to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: He means: set aside money worth what the wood gave, and throw that money away.

phrases.english: They said to him:
There is no redemption for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה and reaches the dispute that step 11 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds that something caused by both a forbidden and a permitted thing is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's requirement to destroy the value of the forbidden wood used to bake the bread.

steps.title: Who are the רבנן who disagree with רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבי אליעזר matches one ברייתא, who are the רבנן who disagree with him and match the other one? The רבנן of this משנה forbid even more than he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן who disagree with רבי אליעזר, who are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own new suggestion. It points out that this משנה does not provide a partner on the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To explain two conflicting ברייתות, the גמרא needs one side that forbids and one side that permits. Here the רבנן do not permit the bread. They forbid all the loaves and allow no redemption. So they cannot be the source for the ברייתא that permits, and the גמרא demands to know who that other opinion is.

keyTerms.meaning: Who disagree with him.
Who are they?

phrases.english: The Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer,
who are they?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַאן נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 11 in light of the משנה quoted in steps 12–13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the wood dispute explains both ברייתות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן in the משנה forbid even more than רבי אליעזר does, so they cannot be the opinion that permits. The second ברייתא is left with no source.

steps.title: The רבנן of the wood case cannot be the lenient opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests whether the רבנן who argue with רבי אליעזר about אשרה wood could be the lenient side, and rejects it because they are even stricter than he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the רבנן of the wood case, they are even stricter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the first possible candidate for the 'other side' and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need רבנן who argue with רבי אליעזר in the lenient direction, so they can match the ברייתא that permits. But in the אשרה wood case the רבנן forbid all the bread and do not even allow throwing the value into ים המלח. They are stricter, not more lenient, so they cannot be the lenient ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility the גמרא will test)
Wood (here, wood taken from an אשרה)
They are even more strict

phrases.english: If you say it is the Rabbis of the wood case,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 12: bread baked in an oven fired with אשרה wood.

phrases.english: they are even more stringent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills out the question of step 14 by testing the first candidate and rejecting it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects matching the lenient ברייתא to the רבנן of the אשרה wood משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those רבנן are stricter than רבי אליעזר, so they cannot be the source of a lenient ruling.

steps.title: The רבנן of the leaven case do not help either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the רבנן who are lenient with שאור of תרומה, then rejects it: being lenient with תרומה does not show they are lenient with עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it is the רבנן of the leaven case. But maybe you heard that the רבנן are lenient with leaven. Are they also lenient with עבודה זרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second candidate, the רבנן of the שאור case, and rejects them too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן of the שאור case do argue with רבי אליעזר in the lenient direction. But their case is about תרומה mixed with regular leaven. עבודה זרה is a much more severe prohibition, so we cannot assume they would be lenient there too.

keyTerms.meaning: Sourdough leaven used to make dough rise
Say that you heard (it is true in one case, but what about another?)
They are lenient

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument about שאור itself. The גמרא only rejects stretching a leniency from תרומה over to עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Rather, the Rabbis of the leaven case,
say that you heard that the Rabbis
are lenient with leaven,
are they lenient with idol worship?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דִּמְקִילִּי בִּשְׂאוֹר, בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מִי מְקִילִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wood רבנן fail, the גמרא tries the שאור רבנן and rejects them as well.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects matching the lenient ברייתא about עבודה זרה to the רבנן of the שאור case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A leniency stated about תרומה cannot be carried over to the much stricter prohibition of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: One ברייתא is רבי יוסי and the other is the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives up on the רבי אליעזר approach and says one ברייתא follows רבי יוסי and the other follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really: this ברייתא is רבי יוסי, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes direction and gives a new way to split the two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no group can be the lenient partner to רבי אליעזר, the גמרא drops that approach and accepts the reading from step 4. רבי יוסי holds that זה וזה גורם is permitted, even with עבודה זרה, and matches the lenient ברייתא. The רבנן match the strict one. So the distinction from step 2 is dropped, and the גמרא must now explain רבי יוסי's strict-sounding words in the משנה. The next step does that.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, really (the גמרא drops the earlier idea and gives the true answer)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבי יוסי as the main source for the rule that זה וזה גורם מותר.

phrases.english: Rather, actually:
this one is Rabbi Yosei, and that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The lenient ברייתא goes with רבי יוסי, and the strict one goes with the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם: הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both candidates for the רבנן are rejected, the גמרא goes back to the reading proposed in step 4 (lenient ברייתא = רבי יוסי). This concedes that רבי יוסי does not make the distinction suggested in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the two ברייתות to different תנאים (רבי יוסי vs. רבנן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתות matched the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא is רבי יוסי (זה וזה גורם מותר), and the strict ברייתא is the רבנן.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's strict ruling was only according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי's strict ruling in the משנה was said according to the רבנן's view. In his own view, זה וזה גורם is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי spoke according to the words of the רבנן. He told them: In my own view, when this and that both cause it, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא deals with the obvious problem: in our משנה רבי יוסי forbids planting under an אשרה, which sounds strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי was arguing within the רבנן's system: since you forbid זה וזה גורם, you should forbid planting even in the rainy season. But for himself, he holds that something caused by both a permitted and a forbidden thing is permitted. So the משנה does not contradict the answer in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words (arguing using the other side's view)
According to me, in my own view
Something caused by both a forbidden and a permitted cause
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי יוסי holds זה וזה גורם מותר and matches the lenient ברייתא. His strict words in the משנה were only said according to the רבנן's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה as his own opinion. He was saying it according to the רבנן's view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, according to the statement of the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: He means his ruling in the משנה that you may not plant vegetables under an אשרה even in the rainy season.

phrases.english: said to them:
According to me, when this and that cause it, it is permitted,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן אֲמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the answer of step 17 by explaining why the משנה seems to show רבי יוסי being strict.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the משנה as an argument according to the other side's view (לדבריהם), not רבי יוסי's own opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that רבי יוסי forbids זה וזה גורם.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי himself holds זה וזה גורם מותר. His strict ruling was only according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רבי יוסי pushes the רבנן with their own rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells the רבנן: since you hold זה וזה גורם is forbidden, you should agree that planting vegetables under an אשרה is forbidden even in the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to you, who say that when this and that both cause it, it is forbidden, at least agree with me that even vegetables in the rainy season are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the actual words רבי יוסי says to the רבנן. He uses their own rule against them to show they should be stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid planting under an אשרה in the summer, because the tree's shade helps the plant. That shows they hold זה וזה גורם אסור. רבי יוסי argues that the falling leaves also help the plant in the rainy season by acting as fertilizer, so by their own logic it should be forbidden then too.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you (your own view)
When two causes together (one forbidden, one permitted) produce a result
At least agree with me
The rainy season (winter)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי himself does NOT hold that זה וזה גורם is forbidden. He is only arguing from inside the רבנן's view, as step 18 explained.

phrases.english: According to you, who say:
"When this and that both cause it, it is forbidden,"
phrases.notes: This is why the רבנן forbid planting under the אשרה in summer: the tree's shade is one of the causes that helps the plant grow.

phrases.english: at least agree with me
that even vegetables in the rainy season are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual wording of רבי יוסי's argument that step 18 said was made according to the רבנן's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling that planting under an אשרה is permitted in the rainy season.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If זה וזה גורם is forbidden, then the leaves' fertilizing effect in winter should also make the vegetables forbidden.

steps.title: How the רבנן answer רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer with רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא's idea: a benefit that comes together with an equal or greater loss does not count as a benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, how do they answer? As רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן would answer רבי יוסי's challenge, and answers by pointing to an earlier statement of רב מרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In winter the leaves do help the plant, but the tree also causes a loss: its shade keeps rainwater from the plant. Since the benefit is cancelled out by the loss, there is no real benefit from the אשרה. So the רבנן can keep their rule of זה וזה גורם אסור and still permit planting in winter.

keyTerms.meaning: And the רבנן? (How do they answer this?)
As (so-and-so) said

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? (How would they answer?)
As Rav Mari said,
phrases.notes: This points back to his statement on the previous עמוד (48b): a benefit that comes with an equal or greater loss is not counted as a benefit.

phrases.english: son of Rav Kahana.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן? כִּדְאָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's challenge on behalf of the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: in winter there is no overall benefit from the אשרה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leaves' fertilizing effect in winter should count as a forbidden benefit under זה וזה גורם אסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The benefit is cancelled by the loss from the tree's shade, so there is no benefit at all, and planting in winter is permitted even for the רבנן.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on this מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned in step 18 that in his own view רבי יוסי holds זה וזה גורם is permitted. So this ruling means: when a forbidden cause and a permitted cause work together, the result is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law follows (so-and-so)

steps.whatToRemember: The final law is like רבי יוסי: זה וזה גורם is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling about זה וזה גורם reaches beyond the אשרה. It applies to many cases where a forbidden thing is only one of the causes of a result.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides' reasoning is explained, the גמרא decides the law.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who holds that זה וזה גורם is permitted.

steps.title: A garden fertilized with dung of עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: A garden was fertilized with dung from עבודה זרה. רב יוסף answered רב עמרם with שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so the produce is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain garden that was fertilized with dung from עבודה זרה. רב עמרם sent a question to רב יוסף. He answered him: this is what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where the ruling from step 21 was used in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plants grew from both the soil and the forbidden dung, which is a case of זה וזה גורם. Since the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, the garden's produce is permitted. The story shows the ruling was actually applied.

keyTerms.meaning: A garden
Was fertilized
Dung, manure
Sent (a question) to him

steps.whatToRemember: Produce grown with forbidden fertilizer together with ordinary soil is permitted, because the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: There was a certain garden
that was fertilized with dung of idol worship,
phrases.notes: This is dung from an animal used for idol worship.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַב עַמְרָם קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: Rav Amram sent a question to Rav Yosef.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: This is what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גִּינְּתָא דְּאִיזְדַּבַּל בְּזִבְלָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling from step 21 being applied to a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יוסי and is applied in practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of רב עמרם's question to רב יוסף about a garden fertilized with dung from עבודה זרה.
